title: Your First Weekend at California State University-East Bay, Shared as Cards
description: A Friday-to-Sunday introduction to the Hayward Hills campus and nearby public spaces, combining campus orientation, recreation, art, local history, and nature.

cards.entity_name: California State University, East Bay Hayward Campus
cards.title: Start With a Campus Map Walk
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Hayward Hills campus
cards.notes: Open the official map and trace a loop past CORE, the unions, RAW, Pioneer Amphitheatre, and the main academic buildings.
cards.short_summary: Learn the hilltop campus layout before the weekend begins.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Hayward campus map identifies CORE Library, both University Unions, the Recreation and Wellness Center, Pioneer Amphitheatre, and other campus destinations.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor routes are affected by hills and stairs; use the map’s marked accessible routes where needed.

cards.entity_name: Cal State East Bay University Art Gallery
cards.title: See What the Campus Is Exhibiting
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Art & Education Building, AE 106
cards.notes: Check the exhibition calendar first, then step into the first-floor gallery while its Friday closure has not yet begun.
cards.short_summary: Use the final weekday window for a student, faculty, or alumni exhibition.
cards.evidence_claim: The university says its 2,500-square-foot gallery hosts student, faculty, and alumni exhibitions in varied media and is located in the Art and Education Building.
cards.access_notes: Visit only during an open exhibition; the gallery lists Tuesday–Thursday hours and says it is closed Fridays and during academic breaks.

cards.title: Browse CORE Beyond the Textbooks
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · CORE building
cards.notes: Locate the popular reading, graphic-novel, tabletop-game, and technology collections so you know what can support future downtime.
cards.short_summary: Turn a library orientation stop into a survey of leisure and study resources.
cards.evidence_claim: The university library lists circulating books, popular reading, graphic novels, tabletop games, course materials, and loanable technology among its Hayward campus collections.
cards.access_notes: Collection access and borrowing eligibility vary; confirm current CORE hours and bring your Bay Card for checkouts.

cards.entity_name: Cal State East Bay University Union
cards.title: Get Oriented at the University Union
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · North and South University Union
cards.notes: Walk through both union buildings, note the dining and service areas, and pick a visible meeting point for future campus plans.
cards.short_summary: End Friday by learning the campus’s central gathering complex.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal State East Bay describes the University Union as a gathering place where students, faculty, staff, alumni, and guests meet for meals, programs, services, and informal interaction.
cards.access_notes: The union’s published academic-semester hours are Friday 7 a.m.–7 p.m. and Saturday–Sunday 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; recess hours differ.

cards.title: Try an Open-Recreation Session
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · RAW Center
cards.notes: Check the live court calendar, bring your Bay Card, and choose an available open-recreation activity that matches your pace.
cards.short_summary: Begin Saturday with a flexible, member-based recreation stop.
cards.evidence_claim: The RAW Center states that one court is generally available for first-come, first-served open recreation and another supports scheduled drop-in recreation.
cards.access_notes: RAW membership is required; consult the current court calendar and building hours before going.

cards.title: Slow Down in the Japanese Gardens
cards.subtitle: Saturday late morning · 22373 North Third Street
cards.notes: Follow the garden paths quietly, photograph without blocking others, and leave food and drinks outside the landscaped grounds.
cards.short_summary: Shift from campus activity to a calm public garden walk.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hayward Area Recreation and Park District identifies the Japanese Gardens at 22373 North Third Street and states that they are open daily from 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m., except Christmas Day.
cards.access_notes: Public hours are 8:30 a.m.–4 p.m. daily except Christmas Day; no food or beverages are allowed in the garden.

cards.title: Read Hayward’s History in the Plaza
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Downtown Hayward
cards.notes: Walk the arboretum paths and pause at the interpretive art addressing Muwekma Ohlone, Japanese American, and Russell City histories.
cards.short_summary: Use a downtown civic space to encounter several layers of local history.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Hayward says Heritage Plaza contains interpretive signs and planned or installed art honoring the Muwekma Ohlone Tribe, Japanese American community, and displaced Russell City community.
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor civic plaza; check city notices for event-related restrictions or maintenance.

cards.title: Follow the Downtown Mural Map
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Downtown Hayward
cards.notes: Open the city’s interactive mural map, select a compact daylight route, and view works from public sidewalks without entering private property.
cards.short_summary: Connect downtown blocks through documented public artwork.
cards.evidence_claim: Hayward’s official Mural Arts Program page reports more than 200 art installations and provides an interactive map for viewing artwork and locations.
cards.access_notes: Plan the walk for daylight and remain on public sidewalks; individual artworks may change or become temporarily obstructed.

cards.title: Meet Hayward’s Native Wildlife
cards.subtitle: Sunday late morning · 1801 D Street
cards.notes: Visit the wildlife displays and discovery center respectfully, keeping voices low and following all staff directions around animals.
cards.short_summary: Start Sunday at a local wildlife education and rehabilitation facility.
cards.evidence_claim: The park district describes Sulphur Creek as a wildlife education and rehabilitation facility with local wildlife displays and lists free admission and parking.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Sunday from 10 a.m.–4 p.m. and closed Mondays; the district notes closures on major holidays.

cards.title: Close the Weekend on a Park Trail
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · 1580 Garin Avenue
cards.notes: Choose a route suited to your group, carry water, review alerts, and return before the seasonal gate-closing time posted by the park.
cards.short_summary: Finish with a daylight hike or picnic in the hills south of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: East Bay Regional Park District says Garin and Dry Creek Pioneer Regional Parks contain more than 20 miles of trails across 5,857 acres, with hiking and picnicking among the listed activities.
cards.access_notes: Gate hours vary seasonally; review current alerts. Parking is $5 when the kiosk is attended, and the park states Garin accepts cash only.
